questions.question: School bus doors must stay closed while driving. When is this rule NOT required?

options.text: When crossing railroad tracks.
When cooling off the bus.
When there is no vehicle next to the bus.

questions.explanation: School bus doors must stay closed while the bus is moving. The only exception is when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should a driver do when dropping off students at school?

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if you leave the driver's seat.
Read while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When dropping off students, turn off the engine. Remove the key if you leave the driver's seat. Always watch the students as they leave the bus.

questions.question: During a driving test at a railroad crossing, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks.
Get out of the vehicle to check for trains.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass other vehicles, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: If you need to back up at a student pick-up point, when should you do it?

options.text: Before students load the bus.
After all students have loaded the bus.
After half the students load, then back up to meet the rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: After all students have loaded the bus.
questions.explanation: Do not back up until all students are on the bus. Watch for late-arriving students at all times.

questions.question: After evacuating a bus, where should students go?

options.text: No more than 50 feet away from the bus.
Downwind from the bus if there is a fire.
Far away from railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: After evacuation, lead students to a safe place at least 100 feet from the road. Keep them upwind from fires and as far away from railroad tracks as possible.

questions.question: During a driving test (except straight line backing), how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle up to two times during testing exercises to check position. For straight line backing only, you can exit one time.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus due to a hazard, what should the driver do?

options.text: Ask students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
Take time to think about whether to evacuate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
questions.explanation: If there is time, contact your dispatcher before evacuating to explain the situation. Make evacuation decisions quickly.

questions.question: If a student may have a back injury, what should you do?

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Do not move them.
Encourage them to stand.

questions.explanation: Do not move a student with a neck or spinal injury unless their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: How should backing a school bus be treated?

options.text: It should be strongly encouraged.
It should be strongly discouraged.
It should only be done in the morning.

questions.explanation: Avoid backing a school bus whenever possible. Only back up if there is no safe alternative. Follow all safety rules when you must drive in reverse.

questions.question: What does ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) help you do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery surfaces.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents brake lockup on slippery surfaces. It helps you maintain control when braking hard. Drive and brake a vehicle with ABS the same way you would without it.

questions.question: After students get off the bus at school, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not worry about where the students go.
Leave once the students enter the school building.
Walk through the bus to check for students who are still sleeping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for students who are still sleeping.
questions.explanation: After students get off at school, the driver should walk through the bus to check for sleeping students, students hiding, and items left behind. Students should exit in an orderly way with the driver watching.

questions.question: When students get on and off a bus:

options.text: It is simple and does not need supervision.
It can be dangerous and must be supervised.
It can happen without the driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous and must be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students die each year getting on or off school buses than while riding in them. Drivers must follow safety rules during loading and unloading. This must always be supervised.

questions.question: If you must drive in high winds, you should:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Drive faster.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: School buses have long sides that can be pushed by wind. In windy conditions, grip the wheel firmly, watch for wind gusts, and slow down. Call your dispatcher if you need help.

questions.question: A passive railroad crossing:

options.text: Has control devices.
Does not have control devices.
Should not be crossed.

questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: When parallel parking, you should:

options.text: Back up past the space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space, then back into it. Get the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as you can. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Honk the horn.
Drive slowly.
Talk to students on the bus.

questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the back

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch passengers inside the bus.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on a railroad crossing.

questions.question: A post-trip inspection should include everything except:

options.text: Looking for items left on the bus.
Checking for sleeping students.
Opening windows.

questions.explanation: After each trip, inspect the bus for sleeping students, lost items, open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The front danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front of the bus to the service door.
